strings.d1.s0.name: CN Tower
strings.d1.s0.tips: A 553 m tower with a glass floor and the LookOut. Book online (~45 CAD) and arrive at opening to skip the queue. EdgeWalk costs extra.
strings.d1.s1.name: Ripley's Aquarium of Canada
strings.d1.s1.tips: A shark tunnel at the foot of the tower. Included with CityPASS.
strings.d1.s2.name: St. Lawrence Market
strings.d1.s2.tips: A market since 1803. Try the peameal bacon sandwich at Carousel Bakery. Closed Mondays.
strings.d1.s3.name: Distillery District
strings.d1.s3.tips: A Victorian whisky distillery turned quarter: galleries, Soma chocolate and a Christmas market in December.
strings.d1.s4.name: Harbourfront Centre
strings.d1.s4.tips: A lakeside walk with canoes. Look out to the islands at sunset.
strings.d1.b0.name: Cluny Bistro Distillery
strings.d1.b0.tips: A French bistro in the Distillery District.
strings.d1.b1.name: Hockey Hall of Fame
strings.d1.b1.tips: Home of the Stanley Cup. An alternative to the aquarium.
strings.d2.s0.name: Jack Layton Ferry Terminal
strings.d2.s0.tips: The Centre Island ferry takes 15 minutes (~9 CAD return). Buy tickets online.
strings.d2.s1.name: Centre Island
strings.d2.s1.tips: Rent a bike, visit the Centreville amusement park and enjoy the skyline views.
strings.d2.s2.name: Ward's Island Beach
strings.d2.s2.tips: A winter walk with views of the icy lake.
strings.d2.s3.name: The Riviera Ward's Island
strings.d2.s3.tips: An island café. Have lunch with a view of the lake.
strings.d2.s4.name: Hanlan's Point Sunset
strings.d2.s4.tips: The western tip of the island: sunset and planes from the airport. Catch the 19:00 ferry.
strings.d2.b0.name: Toronto Island BBQ & Beer Co
strings.d2.b0.tips: A garden venue on Centre Island.
strings.d2.b1.name: Gibraltar Point Lighthouse
strings.d2.b1.tips: An 1808 lighthouse said to be haunted. An alternative to the sunset.
strings.d3.s0.name: Kensington Market
strings.d3.s0.tips: Vintage shops, Latin markets and graffiti. Car-free on Sundays (May to October).
strings.d3.s1.name: Chinatown Spadina
strings.d3.s1.tips: One of Canada's largest Chinatowns. Come for dim sum.
strings.d3.s2.name: Rol San Chinatown
strings.d3.s2.tips: A dim sum classic. Open 24 hours.
strings.d3.s3.name: Art Gallery of Ontario
strings.d3.s3.tips: Gehry's wooden spiral staircase, plus the Group of Seven and Rubens. Free on Wednesday evenings.
strings.d3.s4.name: Graffiti Alley
strings.d3.s4.tips: Street art along Rush Lane in Queen West.
strings.d3.b0.name: Seven Lives Tacos Kensington
strings.d3.b0.tips: Baja fish tacos. Expect a queue.
strings.d3.b1.name: Bata Shoe Museum
strings.d3.b1.tips: A shoe museum. An alternative to the AGO.
strings.d4.s0.name: Royal Ontario Museum
strings.d4.s0.tips: Dinosaurs and Libeskind's crystal extension. Discounted on Tuesday evenings.
strings.d4.s1.name: Yorkville
strings.d4.s1.tips: An upmarket neighbourhood with shops along Bloor Street.
strings.d4.s2.name: Sassafraz Yorkville
strings.d4.s2.tips: Yorkville's brunch classic in a yellow house.
strings.d4.s3.name: Casa Loma
strings.d4.s3.tips: A Gothic castle with a secret tunnel and a tower. The gardens are open May to October.
strings.d4.s4.name: Spadina Museum
strings.d4.s4.tips: An Edwardian-era house next to Casa Loma.
strings.d4.b0.name: Gardiner Museum
strings.d4.b0.tips: A ceramics museum opposite the ROM.
strings.d4.b1.name: Bar Isabel Little Italy
strings.d5.s0.name: Niagara Falls Table Rock
strings.d5.s0.tips: Take the GO train and bus (2 hours) or a tour (~90 CAD). Stand at the foot of Horseshoe Falls. Free.
strings.d5.s1.name: Niagara City Cruises Hornblower
strings.d5.s1.tips: In winter the boat does not run, but you can take the Journey Behind the Falls tunnel (25 CAD).
strings.d5.s2.name: Niagara Parkway Walk
strings.d5.s2.tips: A riverside park. The Clifton Hill amusement area is touristy.
strings.d5.s3.name: Table Rock Market Lunch
strings.d5.s3.tips: A dining floor with views of the falls.
strings.d5.s4.name: Niagara-on-the-Lake
strings.d5.s4.tips: A Victorian town among vineyards. Try icewine tastings (Inniskillin). Take the WEGO bus.
strings.d5.b0.name: Inniskillin Winery
strings.d5.b0.tips: Icewine tasting. An alternative to the town.
strings.d5.b1.name: Skylon Tower
strings.d5.b1.tips: A tower overlooking the falls. Go if the boat is closed.
strings.d6.s0.name: The Beaches Boardwalk
strings.d6.s0.tips: A winter walk by the shore, with snow and the lake.
strings.d6.s1.name: Queen Street East Beaches
strings.d6.s2.name: Lady Marmalade Leslieville
strings.d6.s2.tips: Brunch in Leslieville. Expect a queue.
strings.d6.s3.name: Evergreen Brick Works
strings.d6.s3.tips: A park and Saturday market in a former brick factory. Walk into the Don Valley.
strings.d6.s4.name: Riverdale Park East Lookout
strings.d6.s4.tips: The best free sunset view of the city skyline.
strings.d6.b0.name: Bonjour Brioche Leslieville
strings.d6.b1.name: Tommy Thompson Park
strings.d6.b1.tips: An artificial peninsula in the lake with birdlife. An alternative to Brick Works.
strings.d7.s0.name: Trinity Bellwoods Park
strings.d7.s0.tips: A hipster park with white squirrels.
strings.d7.s1.name: Queen Street West
strings.d7.s2.name: Aunties and Uncles
strings.d7.s2.tips: A classic brunch diner for a farewell meal.
strings.d7.s3.name: Union Station UP Express
strings.d7.s3.tips: The UP Express to Pearson takes 25 minutes. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Bang Bang Ice Cream
strings.d7.b1.name: Museum of Contemporary Art Toronto
strings.d7.b1.tips: Contemporary art in the Junction. An alternative to Queen West.
strings.note0: Pay for the TTC with a PRESTO or contactless card. The UP Express to Pearson takes 25 minutes. For Niagara, take the GO train (direct in summer) or a tour.
strings.note1: Winter brings -10°C and snow. Use the PATH underground walkway network (30 km), the Nathan Phillips ice rink and the Distillery Christmas market (November to December). Niagara's falls partly freeze.
strings.note2: CityPASS costs 130 CAD for 5 attractions. Museums cost 25-30 CAD and the CN Tower 45 CAD. Tax (13%) is not included in prices, and tips are 18-20%.
strings.note3: St. Lawrence Market is closed on Mondays. Kensington is pedestrian-only on Sundays.
strings.note4: Try poutine, peameal bacon sandwiches and butter tarts. The cuisine is multicultural (Chinatown, Little Italy, Greektown).
strings.note5: The islands ferry gets very busy in summer. Book timed tickets online.
strings.transit.name: PRESTO Card
strings.transit.why_chosen: Valid on the TTC subway, streetcars and buses, and on GO trains. A contactless bank card works too.
